question.text: At $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the molar conductance of $0.007 \mathrm{M}$ hydrofluoric acid is 150 mho $\mathrm{cm}^{2} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and its $\Lambda_{m}^{\circ}=500$mho$cm^2$$mol^{-1}$ The value of the dissociation constant of the acid at the given concentration  at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is

solution.text: Degree of dissociation, $\alpha=\frac{\lambda^{\circ} c}{\lambda^{\circ}m}=\frac{150}{500}=0.3$ Given, $C=0.007 \mathrm{M}$ Hydrofluoric acid dissociates in the following manner Dissociation constant, $$ K_{a}=\frac{\left[H^{+}\right]\left[F^{-}\right]}{[H F]}=\frac{C \alpha \cdot C \alpha}{C(1-\alpha)}=\frac{C \alpha^{2}}{(1-\alpha)} $$ On substituting values, we get $$ \begin{aligned} K_{a}=\frac{0.007 \times(0.3)^{2}}{(1-0.3)} &=\frac{63 \times 10^{-3} \times 10^{-2}}{0.7} \\ &=9 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{M} \end{aligned} $$
